lesson.title: Description Agreement Gym
lesson.subtitle: Matching adjective endings to gender: el pastel es bueno, la tradición es buena

hook.title: Harmony Between Noun and Adjective
hook.content: Spanish adjectives echo the gender of the noun they describe. A masculine noun calls for -o (el pastel es bueno, el café está frío); a feminine noun calls for -a (la tradición es buena, la casa es pequeña, el agua está fría).

pattern.title: Two Endings (-o/-a) vs One Ending (-e)
pattern.content: Adjectives ending in -o in the dictionary flip to -a for feminine nouns. Adjectives ending in -e (grande, importante, diferente, caliente, posible) stay identical for both masculine and feminine!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:
exercises.target_answer: bueno, buena, contento, contenta, grande, caliente
exercises.meaning: good (masculine), good (feminine), happy (masculine), happy (feminine), big (invariable in -e), hot (invariable in -e)
exercises.explanation: -o/-a adjectives change for gender; -e adjectives stay invariable.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the matching adjective form: 'La confirmación es ___.'
exercises.explanation: la confirmación is feminine (-ción), so bueno becomes buena.
La tradición es buena — full feminine concord.

exercises.idea: say that she is very happy (emotional state, feminine)
exercises.explanation: Está muy contenta — estar for emotional state + -a for a female subject.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.explanation: La casa es pequeña — pequeño changes -o to -a to match la casa.

summary.outcome: Match -o/-a adjectives to masculine and feminine nouns while keeping -e adjectives invariable.

use_example.german: El pastel es bueno y la tradición es buena.
use_example.english: The cake is good and the tradition is good.

summary.takeaway: Adjectives in -o switch to -a for feminine nouns; adjectives in -e already fit both.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([503] Chameleon Adjectives: listo, aburrido & rico): see how switching between ser and estar flips the meaning of the same adjective!

twist.explanation: La sopa está caliente — state takes está, and caliente ends in -e.

bueno.etymology_derivation: Latin bonus gives English 'bonus' and Spanish bueno (o diphthongizes to ue under stress).

buena.etymology_derivation: Feminine agreement in -a: la tradición es buena.

contento.etymology_derivation: Latin contentus ('contained, satisfied'). Paired with estar for emotional states.

contenta.etymology_derivation: Feminine agreement: changes -o to -a when describing a woman.

grande.etymology_derivation: Latin grandis. Invariable for gender: el hotel grande, la casa grande.

pequeño.etymology_derivation: Romance root *pikk- expressing smallness. Feminine is pequeña.

caliente.shift_rule: Used with estar for food/drink temperature

frío.etymology_derivation: Notice feminine fría agrees with el agua!
